Subject: SLO onboarding: latency & concurrency commitments + warm-pool timeline

Alex / Rachel — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to iterate: 

Summary of what we heard from BrightMart on the call:
- Live-chat style streaming for user-facing sessions; expected average session length: 80–200 tokens, 95th pct session <= 512 tokens.
- Peak concurrency target (initial rollout): 400 simultaneous sessions, target growth to 1,200 over 3 months.
- Latency SLO ask: 95th percentile streaming latency <= 350ms (end-to-end server-to-client token latency).
- Throughput ask: sustain ~60k tokens/minute during peak bursts.

Redwood preliminary commitments / clarifications:
- Baseline capacity: we can provision dedicated pool sized for 400 concurrent streaming sessions with prewarmed instances (warm pool).
- Warm-pool behavior: warm pool allows instant acceptance of requests without cold-start penalty. We estimate warm-pool size of ~20 prewarmed inference containers to meet the 400 concurrency target with expected model (quantized 8-bit) and request distribution.
- Scale-up ramp: if sustained demand exceeds warm pool, runtime will autoscale additional workers; expected ramp to 3x baseline within ~90 seconds under continuous load (dependent on workload token lengths and model).
- Queueing behavior: by default requests will queue on per-instance queues for short windows (up to 12s) to preserve session latency; we can configure a fast-fail policy for strict tail SLAs.

Open items for confirmation (please respond with YES/NO or provide numbers):
1) Can BrightMart accept a warm-pool sizing tradeoff: 20 prewarmed containers to meet 400 concurrency for initial rollout? (we'll share sizing calc)
2) Do you confirm the 95th pct latency target of <= 350ms for streaming under the stated token distribution?
3) Procurement timeline: do you expect contract sign by end of September? Any constraints for legal/SLA wording?

Attachments: BrightMart_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf (draft MAP), warmpool-sizing.xlsx (initial calc).

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa to share a short tech note on queuing & fallback options (action: Marissa).
- Redwood to provide a short runbook showing failover to a lower-capacity model variant if we hit sustained overload (action: Vivek).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive (30m) with BrightMart infra + Redwood runtime engineers next week.

If that all looks right, can Alex or Rachel confirm the 3 open items and propose 2 slots for the tech deep-dive?

Thanks — Karthik

Alex — quick technical note to address your questions. Long version attached; summary below.

Queueing behavior:
- The 12s number is an absolute conservative upper bound for burst absorption when autoscaling is in progress. Typical queuing at steady-state warm-pool acceptance is < 300ms per request.
- Fast-fail policy: we can configure a per-session TTL (recommended 2–4s) where requests that cannot be started within that window return a polite 503 with a Retry-After hint. For streaming flows we can instead keep the session alive and stream partial tokens as we recover (configurable per-route).

Scale-up timeline (example):
- T0: warm pool absorbs first wave (no cold start)
- T0+15s: automatic horizontal scale triggers; new workers begin initialization (container base image cached in the node pool)
- T0+45–60s: new workers report ready for inference (dependent on model loading time — quantized models are faster)
- T0+90s: target 3x baseline capacity reached under continuous sustained load in our tests (we'll share the load curves).

Warm-pool sizing notes:
- For a Llama-3 small variant (our benchmark with 8-bit quant), internal calcs show ~20 warm containers handle ~400 low-latency streaming sessions with median token sizes in the 80–150 token range. Spreadsheet attached (warmpool-sizing.xlsx) with conservative and optimistic rows.

Fallbacks & quality preservation:
- If we cannot meet tail latency, Redwood can automatically route new sessions to a lower-cost, slightly smaller model variant with equivalent functional prompts but lower compute per token. This preserves availability while limiting cost and latency.

Attachments: warmpool-sizing.xlsx (detailed calc), slo-draft-clauses.docx (example SLA wording).

Happy to walk through the spreadsheet during the technical deep-dive.
